terms.longDescription: CLASS is used in object-oriented extensions to define groupings of data and associated methods. It allows structuring code into reusable entities.
terms.notes: Its availability depends on the PL/I compiler implementation.

terms.name: CLEAR
terms.shortDescription: Initializes a variable or structure to zero or a neutral value.
terms.longDescription: CLEAR sets all fields of a variable or structure to neutral values, such as zeros or spaces. It is useful for preparing workspace areas prior to operations.
terms.notes: Prevents data residuals in reused structures.

terms.name: CLOSE
terms.shortDescription: Closes a file or I/O channel.
terms.longDescription: CLOSE finalizes the use of a file, releasing associated resources and ensuring pending data is written correctly.
terms.notes: Must be executed after finishing all I/O operations.

terms.name: COBOL
terms.longDescription: COBOL is used to declare compatibility or interaction with modules written in COBOL. It facilitates data exchange and calls between languages.
terms.notes: Requires respecting COBOL environment formats and conventions.

terms.name: COLLECT
terms.longDescription: COLLECT groups elements into accumulation structures, allowing datasets to be processed sequentially or aggregated.
terms.notes: Its behavior depends on the type of collection used.

terms.name: COMPILE
terms.longDescription: COMPILE specifies instructions for the compiler, allowing option adjustment, diagnostic generation, or control over compilation phases.
terms.notes: Available options depend on the PL/I compiler used.

terms.name: COMPUTE
terms.shortDescription: Executes an arithmetic expression or calculated assignment.
terms.longDescription: COMPUTE evaluates numerical expressions and assigns the result to a variable. It is useful for direct calculations within routines.
terms.notes: Can combine arithmetic operations and mathematical functions.

terms.name: CONCURRENT
terms.longDescription: CONCURRENT enables simultaneous execution of tasks or blocks, allowing leverage of execution environment parallelism capabilities.
terms.notes: Its support depends on the operating system and compiler.

terms.name: CONDITION
terms.longDescription: CONDITION defines states or events that can occur during execution, such as errors or exceptional situations. It allows associating handlers to control flow in the face of such conditions.
terms.notes: Conditions can be triggered automatically or via SIGNAL.

terms.name: CONFIRM
terms.longDescription: CONFIRM is used to validate actions requiring explicit approval. Its behavior depends on the execution environment and the input device.
terms.notes: Can be integrated with interactive interfaces or user dialogs.

terms.name: CONFORM
terms.longDescription: CONFORM verifies that two structures or types are compatible for operations such as assignments or parameter passing. Prevents errors due to format discrepancies.
terms.notes: Useful in modules sharing complex structures.

terms.name: CONSTRUCTOR
terms.shortDescription: Routine that initializes objects or instances.
terms.longDescription: CONSTRUCTOR defines a special routine that prepares an object instance, assigning initial values and configuring its internal state.
terms.notes: Available in PL/I implementations with object-oriented support.

terms.name: CONTINUE
terms.shortDescription: Continues execution to the next step.
terms.longDescription: CONTINUE allows jumping to the end of an iteration within a loop, skipping the rest of the current block and advancing to the next repetition.
terms.notes: Must be used within DO or LOOP structures.

terms.name: CONTROLLED
terms.longDescription: CONTROLLED indicates that the variable requires explicit allocation and deallocation via ALLOCATE and DEALLOCATE. It allows precise management of dynamic memory.
terms.notes: Ideal for structures whose size varies at runtime.

terms.name: CONVERSION
terms.longDescription: CONVERSION specifies rules for transforming data between different types, such as numbers, characters, or structures. It ensures consistency in mixed operations.
terms.notes: Must respect compiler rules to avoid loss of precision.

terms.name: COPY
terms.shortDescription: Inserts the content of another source file.
terms.longDescription: COPY allows including code from external files, facilitating the reuse of definitions, constants, and common structures across modules.
terms.notes: Processed at compile time as textual inclusion.

terms.name: COUNT
terms.longDescription: COUNT returns the number of elements processed or present in a collection. It is used in iteration operations and data analysis.
terms.notes: The result depends on the type of structure used.

terms.name: CREATE
terms.longDescription: CREATE initializes new structures or resources at runtime, allowing the construction of dynamic objects or workspaces.
terms.notes: May require additional memory allocation depending on the created type.

terms.name: CROSSREF
terms.longDescription: CROSSREF generates cross-reference information between symbols, useful for dependency analysis and code documentation.
terms.notes: Produces additional listings during compilation.

terms.name: CURRENT
terms.shortDescription: References the current element or context.
terms.longDescription: CURRENT identifies the active element within a collection or iterative process. It allows accessing the ongoing value without explicit indices.
terms.examples: IF CURRENT = TARGET THEN CALL MATCH();
terms.notes: Its meaning depends on the type of iterator used.

terms.name: DATA
terms.longDescription: DATA marks storage areas containing values, structures, or constants used by the program. It organizes information into clear sections.
terms.notes: Can be combined with other sections like STATIC or LOCAL.

terms.name: DATE
terms.longDescription: DATE allows declaring date values or invoking functions that return temporal information, such as day, month, or year.
terms.notes: Output format depends on the execution environment.

terms.name: DAY
terms.shortDescription: Component or function returning the day.
terms.longDescription: DAY obtains the day of the month or extracts the corresponding component from a date. It is useful for calendar calculations.
terms.notes: Can be combined with MONTH and YEAR for complete analysis.

terms.name: DEALLOCATE
terms.longDescription: DEALLOCATE releases memory dynamically allocated via ALLOCATE. It is essential to prevent memory leaks in programs with dynamic structures.
terms.notes: Must correspond to prior CONTROLLED or BASED allocations.

terms.name: DECLARE
terms.shortDescription: Declares variables, constants, procedures, and attributes.
terms.longDescription: DECLARE introduces data definitions and routines, specifying types, sizes, attributes, and storage modes. It is the foundation of program structure.
terms.notes: Can include multiple attributes in a single declaration.

terms.name: DEFAULT
terms.shortDescription: Default value when none is provided.
terms.longDescription: DEFAULT sets initial values for parameters or variables when an explicit one is not specified. It facilitates the creation of flexible routines.
terms.notes: Must be consistent with the declared type.

terms.name: DEFER
terms.shortDescription: Indicates deferred action until a certain point.
terms.longDescription: DEFER postpones the execution of an action or the evaluation of an expression until a condition is met or a later phase is reached.
terms.notes: Useful in flows requiring synchronization or waiting.

terms.name: DELAY
terms.shortDescription: Introduces a wait or delay in execution.
terms.longDescription: DELAY temporarily suspends program execution for a specified interval. It is used for synchronization or timing control.
terms.notes: Wait time depends on the operating system.

terms.name: DELETE
terms.shortDescription: Deletes a record, file, or element.
terms.longDescription: DELETE removes elements from structures or files, permanently erasing their content. It is fundamental in data maintenance operations.
terms.notes: Must verify that the resource is not in use before deleting it.

terms.name: DEMAND
terms.longDescription: DEMAND indicates that an operation or resource should only be activated when necessary, optimizing memory use and execution time.
terms.notes: Reduces initial overhead in large programs.

terms.name: DEFINE
terms.longDescription: DEFINE creates macros or symbols that expand during compilation. It facilitates parameterization and code fragment reuse.
terms.notes: Macros expand textually before compilation.

terms.name: DELAYED
terms.longDescription: DELAYED specifies that an operation should execute later, allowing coordination of tasks dependent on previous events.
terms.notes: Its usage depends on the program control flow.

terms.name: DEBUG
terms.longDescription: DEBUG activates additional diagnostics and execution controls to help identify errors and unexpected behavior during development.
terms.notes: May impact performance due to extra verifications.

terms.name: DECIMAL
terms.longDescription: DECIMAL declares numeric values stored in decimal format, suitable for financial calculations and operations requiring exact precision.
terms.notes: Avoids rounding errors typical of binary representations.

terms.name: DECLAREDYNAMIC
terms.longDescription: DECLAREDYNAMIC indicates that a variable is created dynamically at runtime, allowing structures whose size or existence depends on program flow.
terms.notes: Must be managed carefully to avoid memory leaks.

terms.name: DO
terms.shortDescription: Starts a code block or loop.
terms.longDescription: DO establishes the beginning of a structured block or an iterative cycle. It allows executing a set of instructions repeatedly or grouping them under a defined flow control.
terms.examples: DO I = 1 TO 10; PUT I; END;
terms.notes: Must be terminated with END to properly delimit the block.

terms.name: END
terms.shortDescription: Terminates a code block or loop.
terms.longDescription: END marks the close of a block initiated with DO, PROCEDURE, or other structures. It ensures the compiler correctly identifies block boundaries.
terms.notes: Each DO must have a corresponding END.

terms.name: DOUBLE
terms.longDescription: DOUBLE declares extended-precision numeric values, suitable for scientific or mathematical calculations requiring higher accuracy.
terms.notes: Precision depends on the compiler implementation.

terms.name: DROP
terms.shortDescription: Removes or un-stacks an object or resource.
terms.longDescription: DROP invalidates a variable or structure, indicating its content should no longer be used. It is useful for releasing logical resources within the program.
terms.notes: Does not release dynamic memory; must be combined with DEALLOCATE if applicable.

terms.name: ELSE
terms.shortDescription: Alternative branch within an IF statement.
terms.longDescription: ELSE defines the action to execute when the IF condition is not met. It handles binary decisions clearly.
terms.examples: IF X > 0 THEN PUT('OK'); ELSE PUT('NEG');
terms.notes: Must accompany a properly formed IF structure.

terms.name: ELSEIF
terms.shortDescription: Additional conditional branch within an IF statement.
terms.longDescription: ELSEIF allows evaluating additional conditions when the main IF condition is not met. It facilitates multiple decisions without needing a CASE.
terms.examples: IF X=1 THEN A; ELSEIF X=2 THEN B;
terms.notes: Must be placed between IF and ELSE.

terms.name: THEN
terms.shortDescription: True branch of an IF condition.
terms.longDescription: THEN indicates the block that will execute when the IF condition is true. It is an essential part of the conditional structure.
terms.notes: Must immediately follow the IF condition.

terms.name: EMBED
terms.shortDescription: Inserts code or data from another source context.
terms.longDescription: EMBED allows including code fragments or data originating from other languages or external sources, facilitating interoperability.
terms.notes: Usage depends on compiler support for embedded languages.

terms.name: ENTRY
terms.shortDescription: Alternative entry point in a procedure.
terms.longDescription: ENTRY defines additional entry paths to a procedure, allowing it to be invoked with different sets of parameters or behaviors.
terms.notes: Each ENTRY must be associated with the same base procedure.

terms.name: ENVIRONMENT
terms.shortDescription: Specifies execution environment or environment variables.
terms.longDescription: ENVIRONMENT allows declaring or querying characteristics of the environment where the program runs, such as system configurations or external parameters.
terms.notes: Availability depends on the operating system.

terms.name: EQUIV
terms.longDescription: EQUIV allows two or more variables to share the same memory location. It is useful for interpreting data in different formats.
terms.examples: DECLARE A FIXED BIN(31), B EQUIV(A);
terms.notes: Must be used with caution to avoid side effects.

terms.name: ERROR
terms.shortDescription: Represents error conditions or related routines.
terms.longDescription: ERROR identifies exceptional conditions that may occur during execution, allowing specific handlers to be activated to control failures.
terms.notes: Can be combined with SIGNAL to trigger conditions manually.

terms.name: ESCAPE
terms.shortDescription: Exits or ignores a sequence; escape character.
terms.longDescription: ESCAPE is used to represent special characters or to interrupt processing sequences in certain contexts.
terms.notes: Interpretation depends on the output device.

terms.name: ESTABLISH
terms.shortDescription: Configures or establishes a context or resources.
terms.longDescription: ESTABLISH defines an operating context, such as condition handlers or prior configurations necessary to execute a routine.
terms.notes: Must precede operations that depend on the established context.

terms.name: EVAL
terms.longDescription: EVAL forces the evaluation of an expression at runtime, allowing its result to be obtained explicitly.
terms.notes: Can be useful in macros or deferred expressions.

terms.name: EXCHANGE
terms.longDescription: EXCHANGE allows swapping values between variables or coordinating operations in concurrent environments via synchronization mechanisms.
terms.notes: In concurrent contexts, it can act as an atomic operation.

terms.name: EXCEPTION
terms.longDescription: EXCEPTION defines anomalous events that may occur during execution and allows associating handlers to control flow in the face of such events.
terms.notes: Complements the use of ON and SIGNAL.

terms.name: EXCLUSIVE
terms.longDescription: EXCLUSIVE ensures that a resource can only be used by one task at a time, preventing conflicts in concurrent environments.
terms.notes: Must be explicitly released to prevent deadlocks.

terms.name: EXTERN
terms.shortDescription: Indicates names visible outside the module.
terms.longDescription: EXTERN declares variables or procedures that can be accessed from other modules, facilitating program modularity.
terms.notes: Must match a definition in another module.

terms.name: EXTERNAL
terms.shortDescription: Indicates objects visible outside the module.
terms.longDescription: EXTERNAL allows variables or routines to be accessible from other program modules, facilitating integration between components.
terms.notes: Similar to EXTERN; usage depends on coding style.

terms.name: FETCH
terms.shortDescription: Retrieves a record or data from a structure or file.
terms.longDescription: FETCH reads a record from a file or data structure, positioning the cursor according to the defined access mode.
terms.notes: Must be combined with appropriate OPEN and ACCESS modes.

terms.name: FILE
terms.shortDescription: Declares a file or I/O device.
terms.longDescription: FILE defines an input or output channel associated with a physical or logical file. It allows read, write, and control operations.
terms.notes: Must be opened before performing I/O operations.

terms.name: FINAL
terms.shortDescription: Marks a block or action executed upon termination.
terms.longDescription: FINAL defines code that must execute when a block or routine finishes, allowing cleanup or resource closure.
terms.notes: Executes even if the block terminates due to a condition.

terms.name: FIRST
terms.shortDescription: First element in a sequence or set.
terms.longDescription: FIRST returns the first element of a collection or indicates the initial position in iteration operations.
terms.notes: Its meaning depends on the collection type.

terms.name: FIXED
terms.longDescription: FIXED declares numeric values with fixed precision, suitable for exact calculations and operations requiring control over the number of digits.
terms.notes: Can be BINary or DECimal depending on the declaration.

terms.name: FOR
terms.shortDescription: Loop with a defined counter or iterator.
terms.longDescription: FOR allows executing a block of instructions a specified number of times, controlled by an explicit counter.
terms.examples: FOR I = 1 TO 5; PUT I; END;
terms.notes: Similar to DO with iteration parameters.

terms.name: FOREACH
terms.shortDescription: Iteration over all elements of a collection.
terms.longDescription: FOREACH loops through each element of a collection without needing explicit indices, facilitating list and structure processing.
terms.examples: FOREACH ITEM IN LIST; PUT ITEM; END;
terms.notes: Availability depends on the PL/I compiler.

terms.name: FORMAT
terms.longDescription: FORMAT specifies how data should be interpreted or presented in I/O operations, allowing detailed output structures to be defined.
terms.notes: Can be combined with FORMATTED for greater control.

terms.name: FORMATTED
terms.longDescription: FORMATTED indicates that an I/O operation must follow a specific format defined by the programmer, allowing precise output structuring.
terms.notes: Complements the use of FORMAT in complex operations.

terms.name: FOUND
terms.shortDescription: Indicator that a search returned results.
terms.longDescription: FOUND signals that a search operation has located a matching element within a collection or file.
terms.notes: Must be evaluated after search operations like SEARCH or FETCH.

terms.name: FRAGMENT
terms.shortDescription: Code or data part treated independently.
terms.longDescription: FRAGMENT identifies sections of code or data processed in isolation, enabling modularization of components and easier reuse.
terms.notes: Useful for dividing large programs into manageable units.

terms.name: FROM
terms.shortDescription: Indicates source in assignments or I/O.
terms.longDescription: FROM specifies the data source in input or assignment operations, allowing control of information flow between structures.
terms.notes: Must be consistent with the file access mode.

terms.name: FUNCTION
terms.shortDescription: Defines a function that returns a value.
terms.longDescription: FUNCTION declares a routine that returns a value, allowing encapsulation of calculations and reusable operations within the program.
terms.notes: Must specify the return type to avoid ambiguities.

terms.name: GARBAGE
terms.longDescription: GARBAGE refers to indeterminate values present in uninitialized variables, which can cause unexpected behavior if used.
terms.examples: DECLARE X FIXED BIN; /* X contains GARBAGE */
terms.notes: Always initialize variables before using them.

terms.name: GET
terms.shortDescription: Reads data from input or device.
terms.longDescription: GET performs read operations from files or input devices, positioning the cursor according to the defined access mode.
terms.notes: Must be combined with appropriate OPEN and ACCESS modes.

terms.name: GOTO
terms.longDescription: GOTO transfers execution control to a specific label, allowing direct jumps within the program flow.
terms.notes: Should be used sparingly to avoid code that is difficult to maintain.

terms.name: IF
terms.longDescription: IF evaluates a logical expression and executes a block when the condition is true. It is fundamental for decisions in the program.
terms.notes: Can be combined with ELSE and ELSEIF for multiple branches.

terms.name: IN
terms.longDescription: IN is used to check if a value belongs to a set or range, facilitating compact comparisons.
terms.examples: IF X IN (1,2,3) THEN CALL PROCESS;
terms.notes: Useful for validating discrete values.

terms.name: INDEX
terms.longDescription: INDEX defines variables used to traverse arrays or indexed structures, allowing control of positions within collections.
terms.notes: Can be combined with DO for structured iterations.

terms.name: INHERIT
terms.longDescription: INHERIT allows a structure or object to adopt attributes or behaviors from another, facilitating reuse in object-oriented environments.
terms.notes: Available only in compilers with OO support.

terms.name: INITIAL
terms.longDescription: INITIAL assigns a default value to a variable at the time of its declaration, ensuring it starts with a known state.
terms.notes: Prevents the presence of GARBAGE in newly declared variables.

terms.name: INITIALIZE
terms.longDescription: INITIALIZE sets initial values in complete structures, ensuring all their fields start with consistent values.
terms.notes: Useful for preparing workspaces prior to operations.

terms.name: INLINE
terms.shortDescription: Inserts routine code at the call site.
terms.longDescription: INLINE suggests to the compiler that it expand the content of a routine directly at the place where it is invoked, reducing calls and improving performance.
terms.notes: May increase the size of the generated code.

terms.name: INPUT
terms.longDescription: INPUT indicates that an operation or parameter corresponds to input data, used to feed routines or processes.
terms.notes: Must be validated to avoid errors from incorrect data.

terms.name: INSERT
terms.longDescription: INSERT adds a new element into a structure, file, or collection, positioning it according to the resource's rules.
terms.notes: May require prior positioning via POSITION.

terms.name: INSTANCE
terms.shortDescription: Instance of a type or structure.
terms.longDescription: INSTANCE represents a concrete occurrence of a defined type, allowing work with independent objects or structures.
terms.notes: Available in PL/I environments with OO support.

terms.name: INT
terms.longDescription: INT declares integer values used in discrete calculations and basic arithmetic operations.
terms.notes: Equivalent to INTEGER in many PL/I contexts.

terms.name: INTEGER
terms.longDescription: INTEGER defines whole numeric values, suitable for arithmetic operations and calculations without decimals.
terms.notes: Precision can be specified using BIN or DEC.

terms.name: INTERFACE
terms.shortDescription: Defines the public interface of modules or procedures.
terms.longDescription: INTERFACE declares elements accessible from other modules, specifying procedures, variables, and structures that form part of the public contract.
terms.notes: Facilitates modularity and separation of responsibilities.

terms.name: INTERLOCK
terms.longDescription: INTERLOCK defines operations that ensure multiple tasks do not simultaneously access shared resources. It allows coordinating concurrent processes while avoiding race conditions.
terms.notes: Must be correctly released to avoid blocking.

terms.name: INTRINSIC
terms.longDescription: INTRINSIC identifies internal functions optimized by the compiler, available without explicit definition. They facilitate mathematical and utility operations.
terms.notes: Available functions depend on the PL/I compiler.

terms.name: INVOKE
terms.longDescription: INVOKE executes a method associated with an object or structure in object-oriented environments. It allows for behavior modularization.
terms.notes: Available only in PL/I implementations with OO capabilities.

terms.name: IS
terms.longDescription: IS is used to establish equivalencies or perform direct comparisons within declarations and logical expressions.
terms.notes: Its interpretation depends on the syntactic context.

terms.name: JUSTIFY
terms.longDescription: JUSTIFY controls string alignment in output operations, allowing text to be adjusted to the left, right, or center according to the required format.
terms.notes: Useful for generating fixed-format reports.

terms.name: KILL
terms.longDescription: KILL ends the execution of a task or process in concurrent environments, releasing associated resources and stopping their activity.
terms.notes: Must be used with caution to avoid inconsistent states.

terms.name: LABEL
terms.shortDescription: Identifier for GOTO or code tags.
terms.longDescription: LABEL defines specific points within the code that can be referenced by jump instructions or flow control.
terms.notes: Must be unique within the program scope.

terms.name: LCASE
terms.longDescription: LCASE transforms a character string to lowercase, useful for case-insensitive comparisons or data normalization.
terms.notes: Operates only on alphabetic characters.

terms.name: LEAVE
terms.shortDescription: Immediately exits a DO loop or block.
terms.longDescription: LEAVE interrupts the execution of a DO block, transferring control to the end of it. It allows early termination of iterations.
terms.notes: Must be used within DO structures.

terms.name: LENGTH
terms.longDescription: LENGTH returns the size of a variable or string, allowing the dynamic determination of the number of characters or bytes.
terms.notes: The result depends on the declared type.

terms.name: LIKE
terms.longDescription: LIKE allows variables to be declared with the same type as another or perform comparisons based on defined patterns.
terms.notes: Facilitates consistency between related structures.

terms.name: LINKAGE
terms.shortDescription: Parameters and variables shared between modules.
terms.longDescription: LINKAGE defines memory areas used to pass parameters between procedures or modules, enabling structured data sharing.
terms.notes: Must match the definition of the called procedure.

terms.name: LIST
terms.longDescription: LIST organizes data in a list format for output operations, allowing information to be presented in a structured manner.
terms.notes: Useful for generating reports with multiple fields.

terms.name: LOAD
terms.shortDescription: Loads code or data into memory.
terms.longDescription: LOAD incorporates modules or data into memory during execution, allowing for expanded functionality or access to external resources.
terms.notes: May require execution environment permissions.

terms.name: LOCAL
terms.longDescription: LOCAL defines variables whose scope is limited to the block or procedure where they are declared, avoiding interference with other contexts.
terms.notes: Its lifespan ends when the block finishes.

terms.name: LOGICAL
terms.longDescription: LOGICAL declares boolean values used in conditional expressions and control structures.
terms.notes: Represents true or false depending on the implementation.

terms.name: LOOP
terms.longDescription: LOOP defines a cycle that executes repeatedly until an exit condition is met, allowing control over iterative flows.
terms.notes: Must include a clear condition to avoid infinite loops.

terms.name: MAP
terms.longDescription: MAP allows data structures to be associated with specific memory areas or defines mapping tables to transform values.
terms.notes: Useful for interpreting data coming from files or devices.

terms.name: MASK
terms.longDescription: MASK applies bitwise operations to select, hide, or modify specific parts of a binary value. It is essential in flag manipulation.
terms.notes: The field size must be declared to avoid truncation.

terms.name: MATCH
terms.longDescription: MATCH evaluates whether a value meets a specific pattern or condition, enabling searches, validations, and comparisons within structures or strings. It is used to determine exact or partial matches according to the defined criteria.
terms.examples: IF MATCH(TEXT, PATTERN) THEN CALL PROCESS;
terms.notes: Behavior depends on the pattern type and the comparison mechanism used.

terms.name: MAX
terms.shortDescription: Aggregation function that returns the maximum value.
terms.longDescription: MAX calculates the highest value within a dataset or among multiple arguments. It is used in statistical operations, validations, and range analysis to identify the upper limit of a set.
terms.notes: Arguments must be of compatible types to avoid implicit conversions.

terms.name: MIN
terms.shortDescription: Aggregation function that returns the minimum value.
terms.longDescription: MIN determines the lowest value within a dataset or among multiple arguments. It is useful for statistical calculations, validations, and lower limit analysis.
terms.notes: Must be used with compatible numeric types.

terms.name: SUM
terms.longDescription: SUM calculates the total sum of a set of numeric values. It is employed in statistical operations, accumulations, and financial calculations.
terms.notes: Can be combined with functions like MEANING or MAX for more complete analyses.

terms.name: MEANING
terms.longDescription: MEANING is used to obtain a representative value or interpret data within a specific context. Its usage depends on the associated structure or function type.
terms.notes: Exact behavior depends on the compiler implementation.

terms.name: MERGE
terms.longDescription: MERGE integrates two or more ordered datasets into a single sequence, preserving order. It is fundamental in sorting and consolidation operations.
terms.notes: Datasets must be pre-sorted to guarantee consistency.

terms.name: MESSAGE
terms.shortDescription: Constructs or handles messages or errors.
terms.longDescription: MESSAGE allows the creation, formatting, or processing of informational or error messages. It facilitates communication between modules and the generation of diagnostics.
terms.notes: Can be integrated with ERROR and EXCEPTION mechanisms.

terms.name: METHOD
terms.longDescription: METHOD defines an operation linked to an object in environments with object-oriented support. It allows behaviors to be encapsulated within structures.
terms.notes: Available only in PL/I compilers with OO capabilities.

terms.name: MOD
terms.longDescription: MOD returns the remainder of an integer division between two values. It is useful for discrete calculations, validations, and partitioning operations.
terms.notes: The result is always less than the divisor.

terms.name: MODULE
terms.longDescription: MODULE defines an independent block of code that can contain procedures, data, and structures. It facilitates modularity and program organization.
terms.notes: Can export elements via INTERFACE.

terms.name: MONITOR
terms.longDescription: MONITOR controls access to shared resources in concurrent environments, ensuring that only one task can use them at a time.
terms.notes: Must be released properly to prevent deadlocks.

terms.name: MONTH
terms.shortDescription: Component or function returning the month.
terms.longDescription: MONTH gets the month from a date or returns the corresponding component in calendar operations.
terms.notes: Can be combined with DAY and YEAR for complete analyses.

terms.name: YEAR
terms.shortDescription: Component or function returning the year.
terms.longDescription: YEAR extracts the year from a date or returns the corresponding component in temporal calculations.
terms.notes: Useful for tenure calculations and temporal validations.

terms.name: TIME
terms.longDescription: TIME returns the current time or allows the manipulation of temporal values in synchronization or logging operations.
terms.notes: The format depends on the execution environment.

terms.name: TIMESTAMP
terms.longDescription: TIMESTAMP represents a complete temporal value including date and time, useful for audits, logs, and event control.
terms.notes: May include additional precision depending on the system.

terms.name: MOVE
terms.shortDescription: Assigns or copies values between variables.
terms.longDescription: MOVE transfers the content of one variable to another, respecting conversion and formatting rules. It is fundamental in structured data manipulation.
terms.notes: The destination format may affect the result.

terms.name: NAME
terms.shortDescription: Specifies an identifier name in special contexts.
terms.longDescription: NAME assigns a symbolic identifier to program elements, allowing them to be referenced in I/O operations, modules, or structures.
terms.notes: Must be unique within the corresponding scope.

terms.name: NATIVE
terms.shortDescription: Indicates native system code or function calls.
terms.longDescription: NATIVE allows the integration of specific operating system or execution environment routines or functions, expanding program capabilities.
terms.notes: Availability depends on the environment where PL/I runs.

terms.name: NEAR
terms.longDescription: NEAR specifies that a memory address is located within the same segment or near area, historically used in segmented architectures.
terms.notes: Its use is specific to environments with memory segmentation.

terms.name: NEQ
terms.longDescription: NEQ compares two values and returns true if they are distinct. It is equivalent to the inequality operator in logical expressions.
terms.examples: IF A NEQ B THEN CALL UPDATE;
terms.notes: Must be used with compatible types to avoid implicit conversions.

terms.name: NOT
terms.longDescription: NOT inverts the logical value of an expression, turning true into false and vice versa. It is fundamental in conditional expressions.
terms.examples: IF NOT READY THEN CALL INIT;
terms.notes: Can be combined with AND and OR for complex expressions.

terms.name: NO
terms.longDescription: NO is used to deactivate options or attributes within declarations, allowing control over specific compiler or program behaviors.
terms.notes: Its interpretation depends on the accompanying attribute.

terms.name: NEW
terms.shortDescription: Creates a new instance or structure.
terms.longDescription: NEW allocates and constructs a new instance of a type or structure, enabling work with dynamic objects at runtime.
terms.notes: Available in PL/I environments with object-oriented support.

terms.name: NEXT
terms.shortDescription: Step to the next iteration or element.
terms.longDescription: NEXT advances to the next element within a collection or iteration, facilitating the sequential traversal of structures.
terms.notes: Must be used with valid iterators.

terms.name: NULL
terms.shortDescription: Null value or absence of data.
terms.longDescription: NULL represents the absence of a value or a pointer without a valid address. It is essential for validating states and preventing invalid accesses.
terms.examples: IF PTR = NULL THEN CALL INIT_PTR;
terms.notes: Must be checked before dereferencing pointers.

terms.name: NUMBER
terms.longDescription: NUMBER declares numeric values without specifying precision or format details, allowing flexibility in arithmetic operations.
terms.notes: May require explicit conversion in complex operations.

terms.name: NUMERIC
terms.longDescription: NUMERIC defines numeric values used in arithmetic calculations and variable-precision operations. It is suitable for data requiring flexibility.
terms.notes: Can be combined with DECIMAL or BINARY attributes.

terms.name: OBJECT
terms.longDescription: OBJECT represents a structure combining associated data and methods, allowing object-oriented programming in supporting PL/I environments.
terms.notes: Its use depends on the compiler and available OO support.

terms.name: OCCURS
terms.longDescription: OCCURS defines that a field or structure repeats a specified number of times within a declaration, allowing arrays or repetitive groups to be created within complex records.
terms.notes: Useful for modeling structures with repeated elements without declaring multiple variables.

terms.name: OF
terms.longDescription: OF is used to express relationships between elements within structures, facilitating references to specific fields in compound declarations.
terms.notes: Its interpretation depends on the context of the declared structure.

terms.name: OFF
terms.longDescription: OFF indicates that an option, attribute, or handler should be deactivated, allowing control over program or compiler behavior.
terms.notes: Complements the use of ON to activate options.

terms.name: ON
terms.longDescription: ON enables an attribute, option, or condition handler, allowing control over events such as errors, interruptions, or special states.
terms.notes: Must be accompanied by a block that manages the activated condition.

terms.name: OPEN
terms.shortDescription: Opens a file or channel for I/O.
terms.longDescription: OPEN initializes a file or device for input or output operations, establishing the access mode and preparing the resource for use.
terms.notes: Must be executed before any GET, PUT, or FETCH operation.

terms.name: OPTION
terms.longDescription: OPTION allows the definition of parameters affecting compiler or program behavior, such as debugging, optimization, or condition handling.
terms.notes: Available options depend on the PL/I compiler used.

terms.name: OPTIONS
terms.shortDescription: Specifies multiple compilation or execution options.
terms.longDescription: OPTIONS allows multiple configurations to be declared simultaneously, adjusting compiler or program behavior in a single instruction.
terms.notes: Must be used with valid options for the compiler.

terms.name: OR
terms.longDescription: OR evaluates two conditions and returns true if at least one of them is true. It is used in logical expressions within control structures.
terms.notes: Can be combined with AND and NOT for complex expressions.

terms.name: ORDER
terms.longDescription: ORDER specifies the sorting criterion in operations requiring defined sequences, such as classification or structure traversal.
terms.notes: Must be used with structures supporting sorting.

terms.name: OUT
terms.longDescription: OUT indicates that a parameter or channel corresponds to output data, used to transmit information from a routine to the outside.
terms.notes: Must be combined with appropriate I/O mechanisms.

terms.name: OUTPUT
terms.longDescription: OUTPUT specifies that an operation or parameter produces data to a file, device, or routine, allowing control over the output flow.
terms.notes: Must be declared consistently with the file's access mode.

terms.name: PACKED
terms.longDescription: PACKED indicates that a numeric value or structure is stored in a compact format, reducing space usage and optimizing storage.
terms.notes: May require conversion when operating with unpacked formats.

terms.name: PAUSE
terms.longDescription: PAUSE halts program execution for an interval or until a condition is met, useful for synchronization or timing control.
terms.notes: Duration depends on the operating system.

terms.name: PERFORM
terms.longDescription: PERFORM invokes a routine or block of instructions without returning a value, allowing repetitive or structured operations to be modularized.
terms.notes: Similar to CALL, but oriented towards blocks without a return value.

terms.name: PI
terms.longDescription: PI represents the mathematical constant pi, used in trigonometric, geometric, and scientific calculations.
terms.notes: Its precision depends on the compiler implementation.

terms.name: PINNED
terms.shortDescription: Fixed storage that must not be moved.
terms.longDescription: PINNED indicates that a variable or structure must remain in a fixed memory location, preventing movement by the system or garbage collector.
terms.notes: Useful in operations with devices or shared memory.

terms.name: PLACE
terms.shortDescription: Locates data at a given address or section.
terms.longDescription: PLACE allows specifying the exact location where data or structures should be stored, useful for hardware integrations or strict formats.
terms.notes: Must be used with care to avoid invalid accesses.

terms.name: PLUS
terms.longDescription: PLUS performs the addition operation between two numeric values, being one of the basic operators in arithmetic calculations.
terms.notes: Can be combined with other operators for complex expressions.

terms.name: MINUS
terms.longDescription: MINUS performs the subtraction operation between two numeric values, allowing discrete calculations and basic arithmetic operations.
terms.notes: Must be used with compatible numeric types.

terms.name: POSITION
terms.longDescription: POSITION sets the location of the cursor within a file or structure, allowing control of read and write operations.
terms.notes: Must be consistent with the file's access mode.

terms.name: POSTPONE
terms.longDescription: POSTPONE delays the execution of an action or the inclusion of an element until a later phase of the program or compilation.
terms.notes: Useful in workflows requiring synchronization.

terms.name: PRECISION
terms.longDescription: PRECISION specifies the number of digits or accuracy of a numeric value, fundamental in scientific and financial calculations.
terms.notes: Must be consistent with the declared numeric type.

terms.name: PRESENT
terms.shortDescription: Indicates presence of a parameter or field.
terms.longDescription: PRESENT allows checking if an optional parameter or field is available, differentiating between absence and null values.
terms.notes: Useful in routines with optional parameters.

terms.name: PRIORITY
terms.shortDescription: Priority level for tasks or resources.
terms.longDescription: PRIORITY sets the level of importance or precedence of a task or resource, affecting its execution order in concurrent environments.
terms.notes: Must be adjusted according to system needs.

terms.name: PROCEDURE
terms.longDescription: PROCEDURE defines a routine that executes a set of instructions without returning a value, allowing the program to be modularized into functional units.
terms.notes: Can receive parameters via LINKAGE or direct arguments.

terms.name: PROTECTED
terms.longDescription: PROTECTED limits access to elements within structures or objects, allowing data encapsulation and control over its use.
terms.notes: Available in PL/I environments with OO support.

terms.name: PUBLIC
terms.longDescription: PUBLIC allows an element to be accessed from other modules or objects, facilitating interaction between program components.
terms.notes: Must be used for elements that form part of the public interface.

terms.name: PUT
terms.longDescription: PUT writes data to a file, device, or standard output. It allows controlling the format, structure, and presentation of information emitted by the program.
terms.notes: Can be combined with SKIP, LIST, or FORMAT for more complex outputs.

terms.name: PUT SKIP
terms.longDescription: PUT SKIP generates an output followed by a line break, allowing records to be separated or report readability to be improved.
terms.notes: The number of skipped lines can be adjusted according to the required format.

terms.name: PUT LIST
terms.longDescription: PUT LIST presents multiple values in a single operation, organizing them as a structured list. It is useful for reports with multiple fields.
terms.notes: Elements are displayed in the declared order.

terms.name: QUEUES
terms.shortDescription: Queued structures for messages or tasks.
terms.longDescription: QUEUES defines FIFO structures used to manage messages, tasks, or events in concurrent systems. They allow organizing sequential workflows.
terms.notes: Its behavior depends on the execution system.

terms.name: RANGE
terms.shortDescription: Valid value range for a variable or index.
terms.longDescription: RANGE specifies the minimum and maximum limits allowed for a variable or index, facilitating validation and preventing out-of-range accesses.
terms.notes: Must be consistent with the type and use of the variable.

terms.name: READ
terms.shortDescription: Reads data from a file or device.
terms.longDescription: READ retrieves information from a file or input device, positioning the cursor according to the defined access mode. It is fundamental for structured input operations.
terms.notes: Must be combined with appropriate OPEN and ACCESS.

terms.name: READ FILE
terms.longDescription: READ FILE specifies that the read operation is performed on a declared file, allowing precise control over the input flow.
terms.notes: The file must be open in INPUT mode.

terms.name: READ DIRECT
terms.longDescription: READ DIRECT allows reading a specific record via its physical or logical position within the file, useful for random access.
terms.examples: READ DIRECT FILE(F) KEY(10) INTO REC;
terms.notes: Requires files with direct access support.

terms.name: READ UPDATE
terms.longDescription: READ UPDATE retrieves a record with the intent to modify it later, locking it if required by the system to avoid conflicts.
terms.notes: Must be combined with REWRITE to complete the operation.

terms.name: READ ONLY
terms.longDescription: READ ONLY guarantees that the read record will not be modified, allowing query operations without affecting file integrity.
terms.notes: Ideal for auditing or analysis operations.

terms.name: READ SKIP
terms.longDescription: READ SKIP allows omitting one or several records before performing the read, useful for controlled sequential navigation.
terms.notes: The number of skips must be valid for the file.

terms.name: RECORD
terms.longDescription: RECORD represents a data structure stored in a file, composed of fields defined by the programmer.
terms.notes: Can include multiple fields of different types.

terms.name: RECORD INPUT
terms.longDescription: RECORD INPUT indicates that the input operation is performed on complete records, respecting their declared structure.
terms.notes: Must match the file structure.

terms.name: RECORD OUTPUT
terms.longDescription: RECORD OUTPUT allows writing complete records to a file, respecting their structure and format.
terms.notes: The file must be open in OUTPUT mode.

terms.name: RECORD KEY
terms.longDescription: RECORD KEY defines the field used as a key to locate records in indexed or direct access files.
terms.notes: Must be unique to guarantee correct searches.

terms.name: RECORD AREA
terms.longDescription: RECORD AREA defines the memory zone where read or written records are temporarily stored.
terms.notes: Must be compatible with the file structure.

terms.name: RECORD LENGTH
terms.longDescription: RECORD LENGTH specifies the total size of a record, useful for fixed-length files or format validations.
terms.notes: Must match the declared structure.

terms.name: RECORD NAME
terms.longDescription: RECORD NAME assigns a symbolic identifier to a record, facilitating its reference in I/O operations.
terms.notes: Must be unique within the file.

terms.name: RECORD TYPE
terms.longDescription: RECORD TYPE indicates the category or format of the record within a file, useful for mixed files with multiple structures.
terms.notes: Must match the file format.

terms.name: RECORDS
terms.longDescription: RECORDS represents a collection of records within a file, allowing operations on multiple data units.
terms.notes: Can be combined with OCCURS for repetitive structures.

terms.name: RECURSIVE
terms.longDescription: RECURSIVE enables a procedure to call itself, useful for algorithms like search, sorting, or hierarchical processing.
terms.notes: Must be explicitly declared to avoid compilation errors.

terms.name: REF
terms.longDescription: REF allows declaring references to variables or structures, similar to pointers but with compiler-controlled semantics.
terms.notes: Must point to a valid variable before use.

terms.name: REFER
terms.longDescription: REFER indicates that a variable or structure depends on another for its definition or content, useful for controlled aliasing.
terms.notes: Must be used with care to avoid inconsistencies.

terms.name: RELEASE
terms.longDescription: RELEASE removes locks on records or resources, allowing other tasks to access them.
terms.notes: Must be used after READ UPDATE or REWRITE operations.

terms.name: REMAINDER
terms.shortDescription: Returns the remainder of a division.
terms.longDescription: REMAINDER calculates the residue of an integer division, similar to MOD but with PL/I compiler-specific semantics.
terms.notes: Must be used with compatible numeric types.

terms.name: REMOVE
terms.shortDescription: Removes an element from a structure.
terms.longDescription: REMOVE suppresses an element from a collection or structure, adjusting indexes or positions accordingly.
terms.notes: Must verify that the index is valid.

terms.name: REPEAT
terms.longDescription: REPEAT executes a block of instructions multiple times until an exit condition is met.
terms.notes: Must include a clear condition to avoid infinite loops.

terms.name: REPLACE
terms.longDescription: REPLACE allows substituting the content of a variable, field, or record with a new value or structure.
terms.notes: Must respect the destination type.

terms.name: REPORT
terms.longDescription: REPORT allows creating formatted outputs for reports, combining data and text in predefined structures.
terms.notes: Can be combined with PUT LIST and FORMAT.

terms.name: REQUEST
terms.longDescription: REQUEST sends a petition to an external module, task, or resource, allowing distributed operations to be coordinated.
terms.notes: Its behavior depends on the execution system.

terms.name: RESIGNAL
terms.longDescription: RESIGNAL allows forwarding a previously caught condition, useful for hierarchical error handling.
terms.notes: Must be used within condition handlers.

terms.name: RETURN
terms.longDescription: RETURN terminates the execution of a routine and returns control to the caller. In functions, it can return a value.
terms.notes: In functions, it must include the return value.

terms.name: REWRITE
terms.longDescription: REWRITE updates a record that was read via READ UPDATE, replacing its content in the file.
terms.notes: Must be used after READ UPDATE to ensure consistency.

terms.name: REAL
terms.longDescription: REAL declares single-precision floating-point values, used for numerical calculations that do not require double precision.
terms.notes: Equivalent to SINGLE in some compilers.

terms.name: RECEIVE
terms.shortDescription: Receives messages or data in communication or queues.
terms.longDescription: RECEIVE obtains data sent through queues, channels, or communication mechanisms between tasks or processes.
terms.notes: A pending message must exist to complete the operation.

terms.name: RECURSE
terms.longDescription: RECURSE enables a procedure to call itself, allowing recursive algorithms to be implemented.
terms.notes: Must be explicitly declared to avoid compilation errors.

terms.name: RELEASE
terms.longDescription: RELEASE removes locks on resources or records, allowing other tasks to access them.
terms.notes: Must be used after READ UPDATE or REWRITE operations.

terms.name: REMAINDER
terms.shortDescription: Result of the remainder in division.
terms.longDescription: REMAINDER returns the residue of an integer division, similar to MOD but with PL/I compiler-specific semantics.
terms.notes: Must be used with compatible numeric types.

terms.name: RENAME
terms.shortDescription: Changes the visible name of an identifier.
terms.longDescription: RENAME assigns a new symbolic name to a program element, allowing interfaces to be reorganized or adapted.
terms.notes: Does not alter content, only the reference.

terms.name: REPEAT
terms.shortDescription: Loop that repeats until a condition is met.
terms.longDescription: REPEAT executes a block of instructions repeatedly until the specified condition is met.
terms.notes: Must include a clear condition to avoid infinite loops.

terms.name: REPLACE
terms.longDescription: REPLACE allows replacing the content of a variable, field, or structure with a new value.
terms.notes: Must respect the destination type.

terms.name: RESERVE
terms.longDescription: RESERVE allocates space or resources for later use, avoiding conflicts with other tasks.
terms.notes: Must be released when no longer needed.

terms.name: RESTART
terms.shortDescription: Restarts a process or execution point.
terms.longDescription: RESTART allows execution to be restarted from a defined point, useful for recovery after errors.
terms.notes: A valid restart point must be defined.

terms.name: RETURN
terms.shortDescription: Returns control and optionally a value.
terms.longDescription: RETURN terminates the execution of a routine and returns control to the caller. In functions, it can return a value.
terms.notes: In functions, it must include the return value.

terms.name: RFUNC
terms.longDescription: RFUNC indicates a reusable function or a functional descriptor depending on the compiler context.
terms.notes: Its exact meaning depends on the PL/I implementation.

terms.name: RIGHT
terms.longDescription: RIGHT allows text justification or values shifted to the right in formatting operations.
terms.notes: Complements LEFT for alignment.

terms.name: LEFT
terms.longDescription: LEFT allows aligning text or values to the left in output operations.
terms.notes: Complements RIGHT for alignment.

terms.name: RUNTIME
terms.longDescription: RUNTIME refers to operations, diagnostics, or information available during program execution.
terms.notes: Depends on the PL/I execution environment.

terms.name: SAY
terms.longDescription: SAY prints text simply, useful for informal messages or debugging.
terms.notes: Does not require complex formatting.

terms.name: SAVE
terms.longDescription: SAVE temporarily stores a value or state for later use within the program.
terms.notes: Must be restored when necessary.

terms.name: SCALAR
terms.longDescription: SCALAR indicates that data is simple and unstructured, such as a number or character.
terms.notes: Contrasts with STRUCTURE or ARRAY.

terms.name: SCOPE
terms.longDescription: SCOPE defines the scope where a name or variable is visible, controlling its accessibility.
terms.notes: Can be LOCAL, PUBLIC, or PROTECTED.

terms.name: SEARCH
terms.shortDescription: Searches for a value in a collection or file.
terms.longDescription: SEARCH locates an element within a structure or file based on a criterion.
terms.notes: A valid criterion must be defined.

terms.name: SELECT
terms.longDescription: SELECT allows choosing among multiple alternatives, similar to CASE or SQL structures.
terms.notes: Must include WHEN and OTHERWISE.

terms.name: SEMAPHORE
terms.longDescription: SEMAPHORE controls concurrent access to resources using counters and signals.
terms.notes: Must be initialized before use.

terms.name: SEQUENCE
terms.longDescription: SEQUENCE defines an order or sequential numbering for elements or records.
terms.notes: May be SERIAL depending on implementation.

terms.name: SET
terms.longDescription: SET allows assigning values to variables or configuring program attributes.
terms.notes: Must respect the target data type.

terms.name: SHARED
terms.longDescription: SHARED indicates that a variable or structure is accessible by multiple tasks or modules.
terms.notes: Must be protected with synchronization mechanisms.

terms.name: SHORT
terms.longDescription: SHORT declares a reduced-size integer, useful for memory optimization.
terms.notes: Its size depends on the compiler.

terms.name: SIGNAL
terms.longDescription: SIGNAL activates a condition or error, allowing the handling of exceptional events.
terms.notes: An ON handler must exist to catch it.

terms.name: SIMILAR
terms.longDescription: SIMILAR declares that a structure is compatible with another, allowing equivalent operations.
terms.notes: Does not imply identity, only compatibility.

terms.name: SINGLE
terms.longDescription: SINGLE declares single-precision floating-point values.
terms.notes: Equivalent to REAL in many compilers.

terms.name: SIZE
terms.longDescription: SIZE returns or specifies the size of an object, useful for validations and memory operations.
terms.notes: Depends on the declared type.

terms.name: SKIP
terms.shortDescription: Skips records or positions in I/O.
terms.longDescription: SKIP allows omitting one or more records or lines during input or output operations, useful for controlled sequential navigation.
terms.notes: Must be used with files or channels that support skipping.

terms.name: SLIST
terms.longDescription: SLIST represents a specialized list structure whose behavior depends on the compiler or PL/I environment.
terms.notes: Its exact semantics vary across implementations.

terms.name: SOURCE
terms.longDescription: SOURCE indicates the source file or module for compilation, debugging, or traceability.
terms.notes: Useful for diagnostics and documentation.

terms.name: SPACE
terms.longDescription: SPACE can represent a space character or an explicit reservation of memory or storage.
terms.notes: Its meaning depends on the context of use.

terms.name: SPECIFIC
terms.longDescription: SPECIFIC indicates that an element belongs to a particular context, useful for distinguishing variants or versions.
terms.notes: Contrasts with GENERAL or DEFAULT.

terms.name: STATIC
terms.longDescription: STATIC declares variables that persist between calls, maintaining their value throughout the program execution.
terms.notes: Useful for accumulators or persistent states.

terms.name: START
terms.longDescription: START activates the execution of a process, task, or routine, allowing workflows to be initiated.
terms.notes: A valid context must exist to start.

terms.name: STATUS
terms.longDescription: STATUS returns or represents the current state of a process, file, or resource.
terms.notes: Its value depends on the queried resource.

terms.name: STORE
terms.shortDescription: Stores data in memory or file.
terms.longDescription: STORE saves values or structures in memory or files, allowing persistence or information transfer.
terms.notes: Must respect the destination format.

terms.name: STREAM
terms.longDescription: STREAM represents a continuous flow of data for sequential input or output operations.
terms.notes: Useful for devices or channels without a fixed structure.

terms.name: STRING
terms.longDescription: STRING declares a sequence of characters, used for text and alphanumeric data.
terms.notes: Can be combined with VARYING for variable length.

terms.name: VARYING
terms.shortDescription: Variable length for strings or arrays.
terms.longDescription: VARYING allows a string or array to change its length dynamically during execution.
terms.notes: Maximum length must be specified.

terms.name: STRUCTURE
terms.shortDescription: Defines a record or composite structure.
terms.longDescription: STRUCTURE declares a set of grouped fields, allowing complex data modeling.
terms.notes: May contain fields of different types.

terms.name: SUBROUTINE
terms.shortDescription: Executable code unit without a return value.
terms.longDescription: SUBROUTINE defines a routine that executes instructions but does not return a value.
terms.notes: Similar to PROCEDURE but without returning a value.

terms.name: PROCEDURE
terms.longDescription: PROCEDURE declares a routine that executes instructions and can receive parameters.
terms.notes: Already generated previously, but included here as it appears in your text.

terms.name: SUBTYPE
terms.longDescription: SUBTYPE allows creating a type based on another, restricting or specializing its use.
terms.notes: Useful for aliases and restrictions.

terms.name: SYNC
terms.longDescription: SYNC indicates that an operation must be performed synchronously to avoid conflicts in concurrent environments.
terms.notes: Complements SEMAPHORE and MONITOR.

terms.name: SYNCHRONIZED
terms.longDescription: SYNCHRONIZED ensures that a section of code executes exclusively, preventing race conditions.
terms.notes: Must be used in concurrent environments.

terms.name: SYSTEM
terms.longDescription: SYSTEM allows performing specific actions of the operating system or execution environment.
terms.notes: Dependent on the PL/I environment.

terms.name: TAB
terms.longDescription: TAB represents a tabulation character or field position in output operations.
terms.notes: Useful for report formatting.

terms.name: TAGGED
terms.longDescription: TAGGED indicates that data includes a tag identifying its type or version.
terms.notes: Useful for heterogeneous structures.

terms.name: TASK
terms.longDescription: TASK represents a thread or lightweight process executing concurrent operations.
terms.notes: Must be synchronized if it accesses shared resources.

terms.name: TEMPORARY
terms.longDescription: TEMPORARY declares short-lived data used for calculations or intermediate storage.
terms.notes: Destroyed at the end of the block.

terms.name: THEN
terms.shortDescription: True branch of an IF condition.
terms.longDescription: THEN indicates the block to be executed when the IF condition is true.
terms.notes: Already generated previously, but appears in your text.

terms.name: THREAD
terms.longDescription: THREAD represents a concurrent execution unit, similar to TASK.
terms.notes: Available only in compilers with concurrency support.

terms.name: TIME
terms.longDescription: TIME returns the current time or allows manipulating time values.
terms.notes: Already generated previously, but appears in your text.

terms.name: TRACE
terms.longDescription: TRACE allows recording or tracking program execution for debugging purposes.
terms.notes: May affect performance if used extensively.

terms.name: TRANSACTION
terms.longDescription: TRANSACTION groups operations that must be executed consistently and atomically.
terms.notes: Must be terminated with COMMIT or ROLLBACK.

terms.name: TRANSFER
terms.shortDescription: Moves control or data between contexts.
terms.longDescription: TRANSFER allows moving execution control or data between modules, tasks, or contexts.
terms.notes: A valid destination must exist.

terms.name: TRANSIENT
terms.longDescription: TRANSIENT indicates that data does not persist between executions or calls, useful for temporary buffers.
terms.notes: Automatically destroyed when the context ends.

terms.name: TRUNCATE
terms.shortDescription: Trims data to a specified size.
terms.longDescription: TRUNCATE reduces the size of a string or numeric data to the specified limit, removing excess content.
terms.notes: Must be used carefully to avoid information loss.

terms.name: TYPE
terms.shortDescription: Declares or references a data type.
terms.longDescription: TYPE allows defining or referencing data types, facilitating the creation of structures and aliases.
terms.notes: Can be combined with SUBTYPE for specialization.

terms.name: UNION
terms.longDescription: UNION declares a type whose fields share the same memory area, allowing representation of data variants.
terms.notes: Only one field is valid at any given time.

terms.name: UNIQUE
terms.shortDescription: Indicates uniqueness in keys or values.
terms.longDescription: UNIQUE guarantees that a value or key is not repeated within a collection or structure.
terms.notes: Useful for indexes and integrity validations.

terms.name: UNLOCK
terms.longDescription: UNLOCK releases a locked resource, allowing other tasks to access it.
terms.notes: Must correspond to a prior LOCK.

terms.name: UNSIGNED
terms.longDescription: UNSIGNED declares numeric values that cannot be negative, expanding the available positive range.
terms.notes: Useful for counters and sizes.

terms.name: UPDATE
terms.longDescription: UPDATE modifies the content of a previously read record or structure.
terms.notes: Must be combined with READ UPDATE for consistency.

terms.name: USE
terms.shortDescription: Specifies the use of names or modules.
terms.longDescription: USE allows importing names, modules, or parameters to facilitate referencing them.
terms.notes: Similar to USING but more general.

terms.name: USING
terms.longDescription: USING declares the parameters or context that a routine will use, facilitating modularity.
terms.notes: Must match the caller's definition.

terms.name: VALIDATE
terms.shortDescription: Checks the validity of data or conditions.
terms.longDescription: VALIDATE verifies that data complies with rules or conditions before being used.
terms.notes: Useful to prevent runtime errors.

terms.name: VALUE
terms.longDescription: VALUE assigns a constant value to a variable or parameter upon declaration.
terms.notes: Cannot be modified at runtime.

terms.name: VARIABLE
terms.longDescription: VARIABLE declares an element whose value can change during program execution.
terms.notes: Contrasts with VALUE or CONSTANT.

terms.name: VARYING
terms.shortDescription: Variable length for strings or arrays.
terms.longDescription: VARYING allows a string or array to change its length dynamically.
terms.notes: Maximum length must be specified.

terms.name: WHEN
terms.longDescription: WHEN defines a branch within SELECT or CASE, executing when the condition matches.
terms.notes: Must be accompanied by OTHERWISE.

terms.name: WHILE
terms.shortDescription: Loop that repeats while the condition is true.
terms.longDescription: WHILE executes a block repeatedly as long as the specified condition remains true.
terms.notes: Must avoid conditions that never change.

terms.name: WRITE
terms.shortDescription: Writes data to a file or device.
terms.longDescription: WRITE sends data to a file, device, or standard output, respecting the declared format.
terms.notes: The file must be opened in OUTPUT mode.

terms.name: YEAR
terms.shortDescription: Component or function returning the year.
terms.longDescription: YEAR extracts the year from a date or returns the corresponding component in calendar operations.
terms.notes: Already generated previously, but appears in your text.
